newsitem.title: CYPRUS: UN envoy sees no imminent breakthrough on Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: UN envoy sees no imminent breakthrough on Cyprus.

text.p: A United Nations envoy on Wednesday played down prospects of direct negotiations between the island's Greeks and Turks to solve the decades-old dispute dividing them.
Envoy Han Sung-Joo, speaking at the end of consultations with leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities, said more work was needed to narrow the differences.

"I have to report to you I feel it would be somewhat premature to call for direct talks at this stage," Han told a bicommunal news conference in the U.N.-controlled buffer zone dividing the capital Nicosia.

He said the purpose of his visit was to explore substantive issues and "probe the willingness" of the rival leaders to proceed in a manner that would ensure the success of open and direct negotiations.
"We need more convergence of views to make such talks successful," Han said.
The envoy said he would report his findings to U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan who would decide on how to tackle the problem.

The eastern Mediterranean island's Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities have been divided since Turkey invaded Cyprus's northern third in the wake of a brief Greek Cypriot coup in capital Nicosia engineered by the military then ruling Greece.
A Turkish Cypriot state declared in the north in 1983 is recognised only by Ankara, which has some 30,000 troops in northern Cyprus.

Decades-old efforts spearheaded by the United Nations to reunite the island under a federal umbrella have floundered, and the dispute remains a source of tension between NATO partners Greece and Turkey.
International efforts to add impetus to the search for a solution have recently gained pace as the island gears up for entry negotiations to the European Union next year.

Tensions in the region flared last month after disclosures Cyprus had concluded a deal with Russia to purchase surface-to-air S-300 missiles, and Turkish threats of military action to prevent deployment of the system.

Earlier on Wednesday Cypriot government spokesman Yiannakis Cassoulides said President Glafcos Clerides was ready to discuss his demilitarisation proposal at direct negotiations with Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash, who heads the breakaway Turkish Cypriot state in the north.
"If there is an agreement to discuss the proposal for demilitarisation, then we pave the road for talks on other, much easier issues," Cassoulides said.
"Right now that particular proposal is not being taken up by the other side," Han added.
